message:
fix(picker): present the picker instead of drawing it where nothing can see it

Once a flip-model swapchain has presented on a window, GDI drawn into that window no
longer reaches the screen, and destroying the swapchain does not give it back. That is
documented for DXGI_SWAP_EFFECT_FLIP_*, and it was measured here first: the window's
own DC held a perfectly drawn picker while the screen held the last video frame,
through a forced repaint, SWP_FRAMECHANGED and a resize.

Three comments in the product said the opposite. One claimed releasing the swapchain
returns the window to GDI redirection, one claimed it hands the window back to GDI, and
one said the picker's repaint is composited -- written before it was true and never
revisited. Together they made a false premise look like it had been confirmed in three
places. All three now say what actually happens.

Only the last step of the drawing changes. draw_overlay, the layout and the hit testing
are untouched: the picker is rendered into an offscreen top-down BGRA surface by the
same code as ever, and that finished bitmap is uploaded and presented through the same
swapchain the video uses. The video stays on FLIP_DISCARD, the device the decoder
shares is unchanged, and the NV12 path is untouched. The picker no longer releases the
swapchain on the way in, which never helped and cost a rebuild on the way out.

Which road to take is not a preference: before the first flip present the window is an
ordinary GDI window and the picker is blitted as before. After, it must go through the
swapchain, and a failure there is logged rather than quietly redirected into GDI --
a silent fallback would recreate the exact symptom this removes.

Verifying it turned up one more defect: a resize never repainted the picker. The class
has no CS_HREDRAW and there is no WM_SIZE handler, which did not show while the picker
was being drawn somewhere invisible and shows as a stretched picture now that it is
presented. It invalidates on a size change while the picker is up.

Measured on hardware with FLIP_DISCARD: the picker appears on screen after a real
toolbar press over a live swapchain, cards remain clickable, three round trips, resize,
wide and tall thumbnails, sixty video frames with zero picker uploads among them, and
the control channel never dropped. The WARP path was not exercised and no A/B of the
video path was run -- its diff is two scalar assignments. Whether the user's original
symptom has this cause is still not proven, only that it has this shape.
